channel.title: AI Proved What? Updates
channel.description: What changed in OpenAI’s math release and the claims AI Proved What? follows.

item.title: Result 379 grows to seven papers: matrix multiplication exponent 9/4, sunflowers, Valiant’s hierarchy
item.description: Result 379 extended: OpenAI retitled it “Euclidean tensor geometry and its applications to complexity and combinatorics” and added seven papers; it says the hierarchy and circuit lower bound papers subsume the November 23 paper “VP and VNP are different” (still available unchanged). They claim: VF ≠ VBP ≠ VP ≠ VNP over every field; circuits for the Hamiltonian cycle polynomial (every field) and the permanent (outside characteristic two) need exp(c(log N)²/(log log N)²) gates, far beyond the bound of 108; the matrix multiplication exponent is exactly 9/4 over every field, a matching lower bound for 107; finite Fourier transforms cost N(log N)^(1/2+o(1)) gates, with a matching lower bound, far below 130; integers multiply in time n(log n)^(1/2+o(1)) on one fixed multitape machine, optimal under variable-count Weak ETH, far below 109; and the fixed-petal sunflower conjecture of Erdős and Rado. OpenAI’s Lean covers parts of each (scope notes); we have not run it. Not peer reviewed. Episode coming Source.

item.title: New result 380: strongly polynomial linear programming, OpenAI claims
item.description: New result 380: OpenAI claims a deterministic strongly polynomial algorithm for linear programming, answering Smale’s ninth problem (also convex quadratic programming, and mean-payoff games: strongly polynomial when deterministic, polynomial bit time for stochastic games with binary rational data, far beyond 104, which it cites); a second paper disproves the polynomial Hirsch conjecture with bounded simple rational polytopes of superpolynomial graph diameter. OpenAI’s Lean covers rational linear programming in strongly polynomial time and the Hirsch counterexamples, not the games (scope notes); we have not run it. Not peer reviewed. Episode coming Source.

item.title: Lean scope widened for 107 and 130; Lean added for 109
item.description: Lean: OpenAI’s scope notes now state, over every field, that the matrix multiplication exponent is exactly 9/4 and the dual exponent exactly 1/2 (107; the earlier comparator file for the complex bounds was removed), and upper and lower bounds N(log N)^(1/2±o(1)) for finite Fourier transforms (130). Result 109 gets its first Lean formalization: its own n(log n)^(1−κ) bound, the new n(log n)^(1/2+o(1)) bound and the conditional lower bound under Weak ETH. We have not run any of it. Lean Source.

item.title: Specials: AN08, VP ≠ VNP over every field?
item.description: Specials: AN08 explains Anthropic’s claim, in a paper credited to Claude, that arithmetic circuits for the permanent and the Hamiltonian cycle polynomial need more than m^(c·(log m)^(1/3)) gates, so VP ≠ VNP over every field: what an arithmetic circuit is, the determinant against the permanent (with examples of ours), what would be new and how slowly the bound grows, the paper’s two-case proof outline, our reading of its Lean statement file, and what is still open: no human mathematician has checked it, and only Anthropic’s own checks have run. Not P vs NP. Not built or run by us. Anthropic makes Claude, which helps make this series. Beyond OpenAI Source.

item.title: New result 379: VP and VNP are different, OpenAI claims
item.description: New result 379: OpenAI claims that VP differs from VNP over every field: an explicit VNP family needs border arithmetic circuits of size at least exp(Ω((log n)^(5/4))), and the same bound holds for the directed Hamiltonian cycle polynomial over every field and for the permanent outside characteristic two. The paper’s Corollary 1.2 also carries the bound over to determinantal complexity, far beyond the cubic bound of result 108, which it cites. OpenAI’s Lean proof covers the exact separation of VP and VNP (superpolynomial exact circuit lower bounds), not the border bound. OpenAI says the result was obtained on November 6, 2026. Anthropic posted a similar claim the same day (AN08). Not P vs NP. Episode coming Source.

item.title: Anthropic posts a claimed proof that VP ≠ VNP, written by Claude, in Lean (not yet checked by humans)
item.description: VP vs VNP: on November 23, 2026, Anthropic posted a paper and a Lean formalization claiming that VP ≠ VNP over every field, which would settle Valiant’s 1979 conjecture, the algebraic analogue of P vs NP. The claim: circuits for the Hamiltonian cycle polynomial, and for the permanent outside characteristic 2, need more than m^(c (log m)^(1/3)) gates for all large m, also for circuits that only approximate. The README says the result “was discovered by an internal research Claude model”, that the 70-page paper and the Lean (by our count 324 files, about 73,000 lines) were written by AI models, and that “no human mathematician has checked the proof”. Anthropic’s own CI, including a comparator run with the independent nanoda kernel, passed; there is no outside check or expert review yet. It does not settle P vs NP or say anything about Boolean circuits. Related: AN03, Anthropic’s earlier complexity claim in the same repository. Our Specials episode is now out: AN08; not built or run by us. Anthropic makes Claude, which helps make this series. Note Source.

item.title: Specials: AN07, the Riemann hypothesis in Lean, checked (follow-up to AN06)
item.description: Specials: AN07, the follow-up to AN06, explains what it means that Levent Alpöge’s Lean proof of the Riemann hypothesis, made working with Claude, has been checked: Kevin Buzzard’s four questions, why the statement must match (with an example of ours), Andrew Sutherland’s checks (zero build errors, only the three standard axioms, independent kernels accepting the exported proof; his checks were run with Claude Code), and the Lean and Mathlib communities’ “full confidence”. It also covers what is still open: the check relies on the kernels and Mathlib’s definitions, and there is no paper, human-readable proof or peer review yet. Not built or run by us. Anthropic makes Claude, which helps make this series. Beyond OpenAI Source.

item.title: AN06: the Riemann hypothesis proof in Lean is independently checked (no paper yet)
item.description: Lean: Levent Alpöge’s Lean proof of the Riemann hypothesis and GRH for Dirichlet L-functions (AN06), made working with Claude, has now been checked. Andrew Sutherland (MIT) published a full build of all 175,187 modules with zero errors, only Lean’s three standard axioms, and acceptance by independent kernels (his checks were run with Claude Code). On November 21 the Lean and Mathlib communities, endorsed by the Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative, said they have “full confidence” the proof is correct, after comparator confirmed that it proves exactly Mathlib’s statement. There is still no human-readable proof or peer review. We updated the AN06 ledger and the pointer on AN02; not built or run by us. Anthropic makes Claude, which helps make this series. Lean Source.

item.title: Specials: AN06, the Riemann hypothesis claim in Lean (Alpöge, with Claude)
item.description: Specials: AN06 looks at Levent Alpöge’s November 20, 2026 note saying that, working with Claude, he found a proof of the Riemann hypothesis and of GRH for Dirichlet L-functions, formalized in Lean. There is no paper. By our reading the Lean statements say exactly that, in Mathlib’s definitions (not the Extended RH), and our text search finds no sorry or axiom; as of November 20 there is no published axiom list or independent kernel check, and a public full rebuild is under way. Related: AN02 (two thirds of the zeros: a result Claude found and wrote, which he and Ralph Furman checked) and 003 (OpenAI’s claimed zero-free region past 7/8). Not built or run by us. Anthropic makes Claude, which helps make this series. Beyond OpenAI Source.

item.title: Anthropic mathematician claims a proof of the Riemann hypothesis with Claude (not yet checked)
item.description: Riemann hypothesis: in a four-page note dated November 20, 2026, Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, says he believes that, working with Claude, he has found a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, and that the method also proves the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis. There is no paper: the note says the argument is formalized in Lean “without assumptions” and links a Lean archive, and says a written version made with Claude ran past 250,000 pages. Scientific American reports that Andrew Sutherland (MIT) compiled the Lean code. No one has yet published a check that the Lean statement is the Riemann hypothesis, and there is no expert review yet. Related: AN02, Anthropic’s earlier result on the zeros of the zeta function, whose result he checked as a listed author. Our Specials episode is now out: AN06; not built or run by us. Anthropic makes Claude, which helps make this series. Note Source.

item.title: Specials: AX10, the minimal model program in Lean (result 056)
item.description: Specials: AX10, Axiom Math’s Lean formalization of the minimal model program in dimension at most four (November 17, 2026), which, by Axiom’s account, formalizes the projective fourfold termination theorem of 056. By our reading the main Lean statement matches the paper’s Theorem 1.2; we did not check the definitions underneath. The README says AI agents wrote it and people have not yet reviewed it, and it rests on the AI-written part of Axiom’s Stacks library (AX06), at the same commit as AX09. No CI or comparator run; no outside build yet. No new mathematics beyond 056; the Kähler papers are not covered; not built or run by us. Beyond OpenAI Source.

item.title: 056: Axiom releases a Lean formalization of the projective fourfold termination theorem
item.description: 056: in a post on November 17, 2026, Axiom Math released a Lean formalization of the minimal model program in dimension at most four, built on its Lean Stacks Project. Its README says the four-dimensional theorem follows OpenAI’s projective paper, Termination for projective log canonical fourfolds with rational boundary: every maximal program for a projective log canonical fourfold with rational boundary over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero has finitely many birational steps and ends with a nef adjoint or a Mori fibre space. It reports no unproved steps and only the standard axioms; the code, about 2,270 modules written by AI agents, has not yet been reviewed by humans. The four Kähler papers of result 056 are not covered. This is Axiom’s work, not OpenAI’s; not built or run by us. Lean Source.

item.title: AX01: Axiom formalizes 30 published theorems on top of its classification library
item.description: AX01: in a post on November 16, 2026, Axiom says Axiom Prover formalized 30 published theorems from outside the classification proof on top of its Lean classification library, among them the Hall–Paige conjecture, a claim from Galois’s last letter, Witt’s Steiner systems and the spectrum of the Tutte 12-cage. In the new repository, each result is proved once with the library theorems it uses as hypotheses and once from the library itself (except Hall–Paige, whose proof from the library is still in progress); its metadata lists the review as self-assessed by Axiom, and there is no published comparator run. Known theorems, not new mathematics; not built or run by us. Source.

item.title: AX08: Axiom shortens the cluster algebra challenge file; code unchanged
item.description: AX08: a commit pushed to Axiom’s ClusterAlgebras repository on November 16, 2026 shortens the challenge file (Challenge/Basic.lean) from 1,981 to 998 lines, to fit Palomar’s 1,000-line limit. The commit message says only comments and layout change: the code is token-for-token the same, and the statements of the 11 challenge theorems are unchanged. The library itself is not touched. Not built or run by us. Source.

item.title: 127: a note on Hexagon claims a smaller constant
item.description: 127: a note on Hexagon (November 15, 2026), contributed by David Niedbala Giraudin, claims a smaller constant than the preprint’s 8d√n: average sensitivity below 2.394d√n (the note puts the previous best at about 3.19d√n), by changing one step of OpenAI’s weighted-grading argument. It cites earlier outside notes with constants below 8 as well. Hexagon labels it “Primarily AI-generated text”; its provenance statement says the work was done with Anthropic’s Claude and that no professional mathematician has reviewed it yet. Not checked by us. Anthropic makes Claude, which helps make this series. Note Source.

item.title: Beyond OpenAI’s catalogue: AX09, Faltings’ theorem in Lean
item.description: Beyond OpenAI’s catalogue: AX09, Axiom Math’s Lean proof of Faltings’ theorem, the Mordell conjecture (November 12, 2026), following Bombieri’s simplification of Vojta’s proof. Its statement matches an outside benchmark problem (our text comparison). The README says AI agents wrote it and people have not yet reviewed it, and it rests on the AI-written part of Axiom’s Stacks library (AX06). No CI or comparator run; partial outside builds only. A known theorem, not new mathematics; not built or run by us. See also AX07. Beyond OpenAI Source.

item.title: 182: Eric Naslund’s preprint claims an explicit exponent
item.description: 182: Eric Naslund’s preprint on Hexagon (November 13, 2026) claims an explicit exponent for the first paper’s theorem: every square-difference-free subset of 1, …, N has at most CN0.9999873 elements, following the same strategy with 72 slots in place of (24!)161. Hexagon labels it “Primarily AI-generated text”; its provenance statement says AI models, including Anthropic’s Claude, wrote it under his supervision. Its partial Lean formalization proves a weaker exponent, 0.99999, conditional on five named analytic inputs and explicit numerical hypotheses. Not peer reviewed; not checked by us. Anthropic makes Claude, which helps make this series. Note Source.

item.title: PSI04: PSI’s paper now cites a different proof by Liu and Qiao
item.description: PSI04: PSI’s PPT-maps paper was updated on November 13, 2026 to cite a different proof, by Ao-Xiang Liu and Cong-Feng Qiao, of its qubit-reference result and the 2(d − 1) composition bound (a research manuscript in their GitHub repository). One sentence and one reference added; the theorem is unchanged. Not peer reviewed. Source.

item.title: AX06: Axiom refines existing formalizations in its Stacks Project repository
item.description: AX06: a commit to Axiom’s Stacks Project repository on November 11, 2026 (UTC; “feat: refine existing formalizations”, #17) adds and edits Lean files, mostly in the StacksFrontier library (374,783 lines added, 43,223 removed, by GitHub’s count; at least 836 files added and 5 removed). The README and the metadata, with its tag counts and review status, are unchanged. Not built or run by us. Lean Source.

item.title: Beyond OpenAI’s catalogue: AX08, cluster algebras in Lean
item.description: Beyond OpenAI’s catalogue: AX08, Axiom Math’s Lean library for the first seven chapters of a cluster algebra textbook (November 10, 2026). The Laurent phenomenon and the finite type classification are in, positivity is not, and cited results and some exercises enter as stated hypotheses. Axiom’s project site says AI agents (Anthropic’s Claude) wrote it; the blog post does not mention AI. Unlike AX07, it has a CI build and a comparator file, but no published comparator log or independent check yet. Known mathematics, not a new theorem; not built or run by us. Disclosure: Anthropic makes Claude, which helps make this series. See also AX06 and AX01. Beyond OpenAI Source.

item.title: AX06: Axiom’s Stacks Project formalization clears its compiler warnings
item.description: AX06: a commit to Axiom’s Stacks Project repository on November 10, 2026 (“chore: resolve all warnings”, #16) makes small edits to proofs across thousands of Lean files (111,608 lines added, 104,048 removed, by GitHub’s count). The README and the metadata, with its tag counts and review status, are unchanged. Not built or run by us. Lean Source.

item.title: AX01: Axiom’s CFSG repository lists a third main theorem and drops its certified-milestone wrappers
item.description: AX01: a large clean-up commit to Axiom’s CFSG repository (November 9, 2026, “Improve code quality and reduce memory usage”) adds CFSG.Certified.classification_finite_simple_groups, the theorem the comparator solution already calls, to the main results in its formalization.yaml (sorry count 0, Lean’s three standard axioms), and removes the top-level CertifiedResults, CertifiedMilestones, CertifiedYardstones and YardstoneContract files. The README, the comparator files and the top-level CFSG.lean are unchanged. Not built or run by us. Lean (noted November 10, 2026) Source.

item.title: Beyond OpenAI’s catalogue: AN04, Fermat in Lean in 30 hours (claimed)
item.description: Beyond OpenAI’s catalogue: AN04, Anthropic’s claim (November 9, 2026) that about 1,000 Fable 5.2 agents redid its September Lean formalization of Fermat’s Last Theorem (AN01) in about 30 hours. Its blog and system card say the agents started from 60 statements, definitions and 47 proved lemmas from the September run. No Lean code is public and no outside check is named, so nothing can be checked yet. Known mathematics; not built or run by us. Disclosure: Anthropic makes Claude, which helps make this series. Beyond OpenAI Source.

item.title: Beyond OpenAI’s catalogue: AN05, an exact limit for the spinless modular bootstrap
item.description: Beyond OpenAI’s catalogue: AN05, “The spinless modular bootstrap at large central charge”, a Hexagon preprint contributed by Anthropic (November 7, 2026) that claims the exact best slope, about 9.1266, of a bound on the lightest state of a 2D conformal field theory at large c, previously known to lie between 8.503 and 12. Mathematical physics; optimality proved by hand, attainment computer-assisted, finer details conjectured. No named human author; one unnamed physicist checked the main results; not peer reviewed; no Lean. Disclosure: Anthropic makes Claude, which helps make this series. See also AN03. Beyond OpenAI Source.

item.title: Beyond OpenAI’s catalogue: AX07, the Weil conjectures in Lean
item.description: Beyond OpenAI’s catalogue: AX07, Axiom Math’s Lean formalization of the four Weil conjectures (November 6, 2026). Its README says the about 980 modules were written by AI agents and not yet reviewed by humans; the decisive weight estimate comes from the unreviewed StacksFrontier tier of AX06. Its README says it proves verbatim an outside LeanEval statement (without the Betti numbers), but no comparator run or independent check exists yet. Known mathematics, not a new theorem; not built or run by us. See also AX01. Beyond OpenAI Source.

item.title: Beyond OpenAI’s catalogue: PSI06, a claimed proof of the Aaronson–Ambainis conjecture
item.description: Beyond OpenAI’s catalogue: PSI06, PSI’s claimed proof of the Aaronson–Ambainis conjecture (November 6, 2026), found, PSI says, with a non-public Anthropic model: some bit has influence at least (ε/d)7, where ε is the variance and d the degree. A 60-page paper by David Turturean and a Lean proof of the influence bound; the recorded checks were PSI’s own, on rented machines and in private repositories, with 0 public runs. Not on arXiv, not peer reviewed, no outside statement yet; the quantum consequences are not in Lean. Not run by us. PSI’s second entry after PSI01–05. Beyond OpenAI Source.

item.title: AX06: Axiom’s Stacks Project formalization moves to Lean and Mathlib v4.35.0
item.description: AX06: Axiom’s Stacks Project repository moved from Lean v4.34.0-rc2 (Mathlib 16edf57) to Lean and Mathlib v4.35.0 on November 6, 2026, a version bump that adapts proofs across hundreds of files (41,892 lines added, 24,538 removed, by GitHub’s count). The README and the metadata, with its tag counts and review status, are unchanged. Not built or run by us. Lean Source.

item.title: Beyond OpenAI’s catalogue: AX06, the Stacks Project in Lean
item.description: Beyond OpenAI’s catalogue: AX06, Axiom Math’s Lean formalization of the Stacks Project (November 4, 2026): about 15.75 million lines, 16,219 of 16,249 formalizable tags counted as complete by Axiom’s own data. About 97% of the formalized tags are in the AI-written tier, which Axiom’s metadata says has not yet had human review. Known mathematics, with counterexamples to some printed statements that are Axiom’s claims; no independent check yet; Lean by Axiom, not run by us. Pairs with AX01. Beyond OpenAI Source.

item.title: AX01 follow-up: two-generation of finite simple groups, in Lean on top of Axiom’s CFSG proof
item.description: Follow-up to AX01: AxiomMath/CFSGCorollary (November 2, 2026) proves in Lean that every finite simple group is generated by two elements, using Axiom’s Lean proof of the classification. A known result (the groups of Lie type follow Steinberg, 1962). About 18,600 lines and only Lean’s three standard axioms, per its README, which says the comparator has not been run. Not built or run by us. Lean (noted November 4, 2026) Source.

item.title: Beyond OpenAI’s catalogue: AN03, Anthropic’s paper with the same claim as 378
item.description: Beyond OpenAI’s catalogue: AN03, “A 2^o(n) Time Algorithm for 3-SAT”, a paper credited to Claude (Anthropic) that claims the same refutation of the Exponential Time Hypothesis as OpenAI’s 378, released the same day. Not peer reviewed; no independent review named; purely asymptotic; Lean by Anthropic, not run by us. AI Proved What? is made with Claude. Beyond OpenAI Source.

item.title: Beyond OpenAI’s catalogue: AX05, the Lyons–White conjecture
item.description: Beyond OpenAI’s catalogue: AX05, the Lyons–White conjecture (Defant and Ono, with AxiomProver): on dihedral groups, speeding up symmetric random clocks never moves the walk farther from uniform when distance uses an even power, and every other power above 1 fails on some dihedral group. Lean by Axiom, not run by us; not peer reviewed. Beyond OpenAI Source.

item.title: Lean comparator files adjusted for result 032
item.description: Lean files adjusted for 032, the rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties. OpenAI's release notes say diverging namespaces in the Comparator challenge and solution were adjusted. The scope notes and the paper did not change; we have not run the check. Lean (noted October 30, 2026) Source.

item.title: Expert review now includes published reviews: 9 results reviewed by OSVerify, plus 378 announced
item.description: Expert review now includes published reviews: OSVerify’s reviews fill the second step for 9 results (002, 041, 069, 074, 086, 167, 237, 306, 340), with the verdicts linked; a review is not a certification. With 378, which OpenAI says a named working group will examine, 10 results now show expert review. Review Source.

item.title: Beyond OpenAI’s catalogue: AX02, AX03, AX04 and AN02
item.description: Beyond OpenAI’s catalogue, four more: AX02, a zero-free half-plane Re s > 31/32 for every Dedekind zeta function (Cureton and Thorner, with AxiomProver), building on 003 and 029; AX03, the Huang–Jiang–Oblomkov conjecture (Huang, Lau and Ono); AX04, an explicit positive density for Collatz, not a proof of the conjecture (Lau); and AN02, more than two thirds of the zeta zeros simple and on the critical line, first found by Claude. AI Proved What? is made with Claude, Anthropic’s AI; Anthropic’s own results are held to the same standards as every other lab’s, using only public sources. Beyond OpenAI Source.

item.title: Lean proof for 265, published by Axiom
item.description: Lean proof for 265, published by Axiom (not OpenAI): AxiomMath/AreaLaw2D (repository created October 16, 2026) says it proves the area-law paper’s Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2. Not run by us; the PEPS paper is not formalized. Lean Source.

item.title: Beyond OpenAI’s catalogue: AX01, PSI01–05 and AN01
item.description: Beyond OpenAI’s catalogue: new episodes on results from other labs: AX01, Axiom Math’s Lean proof of the classification of finite simple groups; PSI01–05, five results by PSI on Open Quantum Problems; and AN01, Anthropic’s Lean proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem. AI Proved What? is made with Claude, Anthropic’s AI; Anthropic’s own results are held to the same standards as every other lab’s, using only public sources. Beyond OpenAI Source.

item.title: 151: Andrey Gogolev’s expository note
item.description: 151: Andrey Gogolev’s expository note “A counterexample to the Shub entropy conjecture” (dated October 11, 2026) gives an elementary account of a construction based on this result’s paper. It is an exposition, not a review of the paper. Note Source.

item.title: New episode: local smoothing in every dimension (079)
item.description: New episode for 079: local smoothing for the wave equation in every dimension, OpenAI’s October 25 paper, with its consequences and its Lean proof. It replaces the three-dimensional episode, which stays listed under Versions. Episode out Source.

item.title: New result 378: the Exponential Time Hypothesis is false, OpenAI claims
item.description: New result 378: OpenAI claims the Exponential Time Hypothesis is false, with a deterministic algorithm that counts satisfying assignments of k-CNF formulas in subexponential time and polynomial space, and a Lean proof. OpenAI says an independent working group of computer scientists led by Russell Impagliazzo, Ramamohan Paturi and Ryan Williams will examine and explain the proof. Episode out Source.

item.title: Result 079 extended to every dimension
item.description: Result 079 extended to every dimension: a new paper, dated October 25, proves Sogge’s local smoothing conjecture for the wave equation in every spatial dimension n ≥ 2, with a Lean proof. OpenAI says it also yields the Kakeya maximal and dimension conjectures and Stein’s spherical restriction estimates. By our reading it implies the claims of 074 and 078 and the sphere and paraboloid cases of 077. Its new episode is out. Revised Source.

item.title: Lean proof added for result 032
item.description: Lean proof added for 032, the rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties. Its scope notes leave out the consequences for the Tate and Hodge standard conjectures. Lean Source.

item.title: Code restored for result 266
item.description: Code restored for 266: OpenAI restored the C++ source and saved numerical records for the computation that excludes a fourth mutually unbiased basis in dimension six, with a Python checker. Source.

item.title: 109: David Harvey’s note
item.description: 109: David Harvey’s note (October 20, 2026) on the construction: he has not checked most of the details but thinks the claimed bound is plausible. Note (noted October 27, 2026) Source.

item.title: 246: Mario Bonk’s seminar talk on the proof
item.description: 246: Mario Bonk’s talk “The AI Proof of Cannon’s conjecture” in the Quasiworld seminar (October 22, 2026); no written review yet. Note (noted October 27, 2026) Source.

item.title: Three papers withdrawn, 14 revised
item.description: Three papers withdrawn after a sign error in “Algebraicity of Weil classes on split abelian eightfolds” and two papers that depend on it; 14 other manuscripts revised and 6 Lean formalizations added. The catalogue now holds 719 manuscripts in 372 results. Withdrawn Source.

item.title: OpenAI’s math release: 722 manuscripts in 372 results
item.description: OpenAI’s math release: github.com/openai/math opens with 722 manuscripts in 372 result families. Source.

item.title: Special S01: finite-time blowup for Navier–Stokes and Euler
item.description: Announced outside the math release: finite-time blowup for Navier–Stokes and Euler, two papers with Lean proofs in openai/NavierStokesAndEuler. Special Source.
